$comment: Violation ratchet for gates whose dead scan root was repaired. A repair REVEALS pre-existing debt; it does not create it. Each entry records the count revealed at repair time — the gate fails only when its count RISES. Lowering a count is a normal commit; raising one is a defect. Entries expire: a baseline that has not dropped within 56 days of `landed` (or of `reaffirmed.date`) fails its gate, because a number that never moves is suppression with extra steps. Mechanism + rationale: src/scripts/_lib/gate_baseline.ts. Decision: AI council 2026-08-02, roadmap road-to-gates-that-can-fail blocker `dead-gate-finding-triage`.

check_gate_completeness.note: Ledger adoption ratchet. Gates registered under the CI task roots that carry neither per-target completeness accounting (`_lib/gate_ledger.ts`) nor a `// ledger-exempt:` marker. This is deliberately NOT a sweep: road-to-skill-ecosystem-gate-integrity Phase 1 adopts exactly three gates (lint_framework_leakage, check_references, lint_roadmap_complexity) plus the checker itself to prove the interface, and the remainder migrates as gates are touched. Shrink-only from here — the number may not grow, so a NEW gate must adopt or exempt. Lowered 216 -> 215 on 2026-08-17 by discharging the obligation three NEW arrivals had incurred, which is the standing rule being enforced rather than a drain: the registered population grew 244 -> 258 and three of the fourteen arrivals adopted nothing — `build_archive_index`, `check_gate_coverage`, `check_pr_ci_current`. The reading was 218 against this baseline of 216, and the missing arithmetic is that one PRE-existing gate (`lint_rule_skill_pack_reach`) had adopted in the meantime: 216 + 3 - 1 = 218. All three adopted a real ledger. `check_pr_ci_current` first took a reasoned exemption claiming no target population; the completion review refuted it from the file itself — the check rows ARE a population, and rows whose `state` is not a string were being dropped before any verdict ran, so a dropped row could be the failing one. The exemption was withdrawn and the ledger adopted, counting kept rows as read, dropped rows as skips, and rows a pre-row verdict never reached as out of scope. The denominator in this note was 14 stale (it said 244) and is now expressed without one, because a count pinned to a population that grows weekly rots faster than the count itself. Note what this lowering does NOT buy: headroom is zero either way, so the next un-adopted arrival reds this gate immediately — which is the intended behaviour and the reason the number is not padded. The refreshed `landed` is load-bearing rather than bookkeeping: `checkRatchet` returns `improved` BEFORE it evaluates staleness, so an entry left at 216 while the tree measures 215 would never expire at any age (pinned by tests/lib/gate_baseline.test.ts, which asserts `improved` at landed + STALE_AFTER_DAYS + 400 days) — the greenest available state and the worst, since it switches off the anti-fossilization clause exactly when someone has done real work. Lowered 215 -> 214 on 2026-08-30 by the same standing rule, and the arithmetic is worth stating because a new gate normally moves this number the OTHER way: `lint_metric_consumers` arrived registered, and it adopted a real ledger in the change that added it rather than spending the slot. The registered population grew by one and the non-adopter count fell by one. `landed` is refreshed for the reason the previous entry records: `checkRatchet` returns `improved` before it evaluates staleness, so a count left at 215 while the tree measures 214 would never expire at any age — the greenest available state and the worst.

check_source_size_budget.reason: Lowered 18,230 -> 18,209 on 2026-09-03 by drain/artifact-location. `doctor --strict` needed 16 lines of integration wiring in cmd_doctor.ts, which sits ~2,100 lines PAST the 1500 cap so every line there costs one excess. An AI council on the residual split (a: raise by 15 / d: descope the feature); neither was taken, because a parallel branch demonstrated the same day that paying down is achievable in this codebase, which is the evidence the split lacked. This gate's own test comment prescribes it: a commit that splits a god-file lowers the excess and must carry the lowered baseline. MERGE RECONCILIATION 2026-09-03, 18,209 -> 18,205: drain/wired-instruments and drain/artifact-location each lowered from the SAME 18,230 base in parallel -- the branch to 18,226 (net -4, run_continuation_hook.ts's termination ladder moved to _lib/continuation_ladder.ts and runtime_journal.ts's prose to _lib/outcome_vocabularies.ts, both under the cap) and main to 18,209 (net -21, the doctor --strict split above). Taking either side alone is wrong in a different direction: main's value silently discards the branch's earned -4, and the branch's value RAISES the baseline against main and weakens the gate. The committed number is neither -- it is the gate's own output on the merged tree, where both reductions apply. THIS LOCAL READING IS ADMISSIBLE HERE, and the discriminator matters because this file's ci-parity:local-only entry records a 165 -> 164 lowering that was reverted for exactly the opposite case: that count depends on how the environment resolves the projection surface, whereas this gate walks only SOURCE_ROOTS = ['src'] (check_source_size_budget.ts:88) counting excess lines over the 1500 ceiling, and `git status --porcelain -uall -- src/` reported ZERO untracked files, so a clean CI checkout of this commit measures the same 18,205. If CI reads anything else, CI's number is the correct one and this note is the record of why. LOWERED 18,205 -> 18,193 on 2026-09-03 by fix/release-curation-ask. The change adds a fifth publication guard, and its own additions landed at +10 excess: release.ts 2,008 -> 2,018, every line of which is past the 1500 cap. ci-parity:local-only.note: Gates that `task ci` runs and no workflow does — the direction this manifest's own header calls the one that let real defects merge (16 stale index rows reached the trunk behind a local-only check-index). Revealed, not created, by repairing the checker's extraction: check_ci_local_parity built its CI-side set by regexing RAW workflow text for `task <name>` and expanding each closure, comments included. Several workflow comments contain the literal string `task ci` while stating that no workflow invokes it, so `ci` was read as an invocation and its full 247-gate closure entered the 'runs in CI' set. The count was therefore 0 BY CONSTRUCTION, and the prose documenting the gap was what suppressed it. Measured at the repair: CI-side 273 → 106, undeclared_local_only 0 → 167 of 247 local gates (68%). Baselined rather than hard-failed because 167 findings nobody can clear in the change that reveals them is the gate-that-lands-as-N-instant-blockers failure this repository has refused before; shrink-only keeps the property that matters, namely that a NEW gate registered in `task ci` with no workflow reds immediately. Lowering happens by wiring gates into workflows or declaring them under `local_only:` with a reason. Note the punchline, because it bounds the risk of this entry: check_ci_local_parity ITSELF runs in no workflow, so it is its own finding and this ratchet has no remote reach either — clearing the backlog is what gives it teeth. DRAINED BY ONE, 2026-08-13: check_ci_local_parity itself was wired into consistency.yml, so it left the set it exists to report. That is the whole shape of a legitimate drain here — the gate stops being local-only because a workflow now runs it, not because the declaration list grew. The floor in gate-coverage.yml moved in the same change and for the same reason: wiring two gates raised the parsed population 357 -> 360 (109 CI + 251 local). The intermediate 359 was the reading after the CI-side wiring alone and before check_gate_coverage joined the local `ci` chain; it was committed here by mistake and is corrected rather than left as a second number for the same measurement. WALKED DOWN 166 -> 165 on 2026-08-20 (road-to-session-closeout 5.2): check_ci_local_parity reported `ci-parity:local-only: 165 violation(s), baseline 166 - ratchet is loose` and asked for exactly this, so the gain cannot be silently given back. The measurement is the gate's own output on the merged tree, not a branch. What is NOT done here is the classification the same step asks for: 165 gates each need a recorded class (belongs-in-CI / developer-aid / dead), which is per-gate judgement, and migrating them would red the trunk on the landing day - the step forbids it for that reason. ATTEMPTED 165 -> 164 on 2026-08-24 and REVERTED in the same change, recorded because the mistake is instructive rather than embarrassing. A local run of check_ci_local_parity reported the ratchet LOOSE at 164 and asked to be lowered; CI then measured 165 and red the gate at '1 new'. The local reading was environment-dependent -- the drain worktree resolves the projection surface differently from a clean checkout, which is the same worktree divergence check_rule_projection_integrity shows on the same tree -- so the number was never real slack. THE RULE THIS CONFIRMS: this baseline is walked down on a reading from the ENFORCING environment, never on a local one, exactly as the 166 -> 165 paragraph above says ('the measurement is the gate's own output on the merged tree, not a branch'). A gate inviting a lowering is not evidence that the lowering is correct.

Deliberately NOT an adoption column ratcheted upward: check_gate_coverage.ts's own report_hardening_ratchet rejects that shape in this same file ("grades the solution instead of the problem"), and the sibling adoption ratchet (check_gate_completeness) is already a non-adopter count. Population is the manifest, not every script under src/scripts: padding the manifest to move this number would mean adding a floor per row. Shrink-only from here — a NEW registered gate must adopt or exempt. Migration mechanism, same as the ledger ratchet above: gates adopt as they are touched, not in a sweep — the eight current adopters were each added alongside a real change to that gate. The 56-day non-stagnation clause applies unchanged, so a count parked here fails on its own.

lint_provenance_vocabulary:permanence-la.note:
Permanence language in an ADR record's load-bearing positions -- its `# ` title, its `decision:` frontmatter slug, its `## Decision` section, or an `Addendum` heading. Revealed by adding rule 4 to lint_provenance_vocabulary, not created by it: ADR-240 section 6 states the doctrine (`forever`, `permanently`, `never revisit`, `never reconsider` and their kin do not belong in a mechanism decision's title, slug or Decision section) and the corpus had five records violating it on the day the rule landed. Baselined rather than hard-failed because a gate that lands as five instant blockers is the shape this repository has already refused (see ci-parity:local-only and lint_roadmap_blockers:decidability above), and every one of the five is a content decision rather than a copy edit: ADR-208 (slug `dist-agent-src-keep-forever`, title "kept forever", Decision "KEEP -- permanently") is the standing self-contradiction ADR-240 cites, since lines 10-11 of its own frontmatter carry the conditions under which it should be reopened; ADR-107:37 and ADR-108:5/12/24/29 are owner PURPOSE statements ("open-source forever", "now or in the future", "liability disclaimer is permanent") whose fix is the escape ADR-240 names -- record `authority_basis: owner_intent` -- which is an owner ruling, not an agent edit; ADR-122:77/154 and ADR-124:229 assert a permanently-off default whose honest form is a default-off setting plus a reopen condition. The rule is deliberately SCOPED and the scoping is the gate: the same word list applied to whole files matches many more, and the large majority are legitimate. The comparison figure is given with its method because 'unscoped' has two readings and an earlier version of this note picked one without saying which, giving 41 lines across 30 records which reproduces neither way: the bare word list over both ADR surfaces matches 45 lines in 26 records, and the word list PLUS the lint's own line filters (code fences, quoted spans, table rows, in-sentence negation, attributive `permanent`, hyphen compounds) but WITHOUT position scoping matches 29 in 17. Scoping to the four load-bearing positions takes it to 11 in 5. The 29-to-11 step is what the scoping buys; the 45 is what a naive grep would report -- an `## Alternatives considered` entry rejecting a permanence option (ADR-105:97, ADR-137:148-151, ADR-212:133), a `## Consequences` line reporting one (ADR-136:90, ADR-208:73, ADR-216:278/298), a `## Context` recounting one (ADR-042:36, ADR-232:34), a quoted open question (ADR-201:342/343) and a table rationale cell bounding a failure mode (ADR-074:41, ADR-225:64) are all describing a permanence claim rather than making one. Shrink-only from here, which is the property that matters: a NEW record asserting permanence in any of the four positions reds this gate immediately, and headroom is zero. Lowering happens one record at a time -- convert an owner purpose statement to `authority_basis: owner_intent`, or restate a mechanism decision with the reopen condition it already carries. The 56-day expiry is the point rather than a hazard: if this number has not moved in two months, the doctrine is not being applied and the gate should fail until someone decides whether it is real.

WALKED 11 -> 5 on 2026-08-22 by road-to-evidence-based-adr-governance 4.3, and the split is exactly the one this note predicted: the six AGENT-EXECUTABLE hits are fixed and the five OWNER-RESERVED ones are untouched. ADR-208's slug is now `dist-agent-src-is-the-shipped-projection-tree`, its title says "until its `review_trigger` fires", and its Decision reads "KEEP, until `review_trigger` (a), (b) or (c) fires" -- the escape ADR-240 section 6 names, taken against reopen conditions the record's own frontmatter already carried, which is why it needed no new judgement. ADR-122:77/154 and ADR-124:229 asserted a permanently-off default; each now states default-off plus the reopen condition its own measurement supplies (for ADR-122, a re-run clearing both locked thresholds with the FP control held; for ADR-124, the category limit behind the null being shown not to hold). Those two carry no `review_trigger` at all -- both predate the 2026-07-25 requirement -- so the condition was derived from the measurement in the record rather than restated from frontmatter, and that difference is recorded because it is the weaker of the two moves. The FILE NAME of ADR-208 is deliberately unchanged: no gate couples the `decision:` slug to the filename (regenerate_index reads the slug only as a fallback when `decision:` is absent), and renaming would rewrite eight inbound references, two of them inside frozen review-input diffs and one inside an archived roadmap whose path was correct when written -- rewriting history to fix a name, which is the trade this tree already refused for out-of-directory decision records. The remaining five are ADR-107:37 and ADR-108:5/12/24/29, owner PURPOSE statements whose fix is `authority_basis: owner_intent`; they are routed to stubs/road-to-owner-authority-decisions.md and are not agent-editable. Zero headroom still holds for the four load-bearing positions.

lint_settings_classes:derivable-surface.note: Anti-regrowth ratchet for the settings disposition axis. 83 of 134 template leaves are classified `derivable` — the mechanism can decide from the situation, so the key should not exist — and each names the replacement that would decide instead (`lint_settings_classes` rejects the bare label, which is what keeps the class from becoming a synonym for "inconvenient to keep"). This is a DELETION QUEUE, not 83 deletions: a row stays until the mechanism it names actually exists, and deleting a key ahead of its mechanism is a silently-changed default rather than a simplification. Shrink-only from here, which is the anti-regrowth half — a NEW key classified `derivable` raises the number and reds, so a key whose answer the situation already carries cannot be added at all. The 56-day non-stagnation clause is the other half and is wanted here rather than tolerated: a queue that never drains is a stated direction nobody is walking. The queue opened at 88 of 140 on 2026-08-12 and drained to 83 of 134 the same day: six keys had no reader whatsoever (telegraph.speak_scope, chat_history.max_size_kb, chat_history.on_overflow, quality.wait_for_remote_ci, screenshots.data_bearing_gate, legal_review_prep.consented_at), five of them `derivable` and one a `consent` row reclassified because a published-egress confirmation is a Hard Floor no setting may lift. An unread key is the only deletion that cannot silently change a default, which is why that batch went first. The classification itself is docs/contracts/settings-classes.md.

check_no_external_sources:shape-block.falsifier: ./scripts-run src/scripts/check_no_external_sources  # the 'attribution shape' line names the current block count; the gate fails when it RISES above this entry
check_no_external_sources:shape-block.note: Lowered 243 -> 148 on 2026-08-30 by road-to-source-silence-cutover step 3.1. AI COUNCIL 2026-08-30, 2/2 seats present (anthropic + openai), option (a): NARROW the `source-header` class, do not delete it, and lower the baseline to the new measured total. REASON THE OLD NUMBER WAS WRONG, not merely high: the class flagged the VALUE of every `**Source:**` header that was not an ENC1 token or an opaque round id, so a correctly ANONYMISED header scored exactly like a leaking one. All 95 findings were read; not one named an external source in readable form, and six were flagging the anonymisation notice itself. One seat: the detector penalised correct behaviour. WHAT CHANGED: `sourceHeaderHits` now flags only a value carrying a readable identifier - an owner/repo slug, a domain, or an @scope/package - per the operational grammar in `readableIdentifierIn`, written out because a seat warned that 'readable slug' left unspecified 'merely moves subjective classification into code'. Both seats REFUSED option (c), deleting the class: a `**Source:**` header is where policy tells authors to record attribution and is therefore the highest-value place to keep looking. THE DELTA IS AUDITED: 148 = 127 tmp-quote + 21 repo-slug, and a full-tree recount removed exactly the 95 audited source-header findings and ADDED ZERO. The first run produced 150, on two middle-of-path segments (`uncondensed/rules`, `installer/src`) that read like slugs; both are pinned as fixtures. EVIDENCE: `tests/scripts/source_header_narrowing.test.ts` over three labeled fixtures under `tests/fixtures/source-headers/` - compliant (must not flag), internal-ref (must not flag), leaking (MUST flag, all three identifier shapes). The pre-narrowing predicate is kept as `legacySourceHeaderHits` and shadow-reported by the gate; it enforces nothing. ROLLBACK, as specified: revert the matcher and restore 243 if a readable identifier in a `**Source:**` fixture escapes detection, if the full-tree count is not reproducibly 148, or if the delta contains anything outside the audited source-header set. WHAT REMAINS IS REAL DEBT: 127 quoted speaking inbox-directory names and 21 repository slugs, 152 of them in `agents/roadmaps/archive/`. Paying it down is in-place redaction under ADR-250, which this change deliberately did not attempt. EXPIRY: 56 days from `landed`, i.e. 2026-10-25. HONEST LIMIT, added on the completion review that measured it: the narrowed `source-header` class now contributes ZERO of the 148 in-tree findings — 148 is 127 tmp-quote + 21 repo-slug — so IN THIS TREE it is operationally indistinguishable from option (c), deleting it, which both council seats refused. What separates them is the fixture corpus and nothing else, and the same review found the first corpus unrepresentative: it missed the most natural citation shape there is, a FILE inside an external repository (`somevendor/some-suite/skills/foo.md`), because the matcher judged a slug by the characters either side of it rather than by the whole token. The corpus now covers that shape in both directions, and the grammar tokenises. Nothing will notice if the class silently stops firing on real content — only the fixtures will, which is why they are the deliverable rather than a nicety.

lint_carrier_integrity.note: 243 pre-contract usages of `[~]` in archived roadmaps that carry no `deferred-resolution:` annotation. The annotation contract was settled by council on 2026-08-27; every file in this population predates it, the oldest by months (agents/roadmaps/archive/step-99-north-star-restructure.md:92 is 2026-05 and uses the glyph to mean 'partially green, not a regression'). They are NOT repaired: rewriting an archived roadmap's step semantics retroactively invents an intent nobody recorded, and the honest alternative glyph `[-]` is owner-reserved (archive_completed_roadmaps.ts:396). Shrink-only from here, one owner decision at a time. This ratchet covers ONLY the unannotated class; the broken-destination class -- a receiver deleted, renamed, re-parented, skipped, or archived with open steps -- is a hard failure at zero with no baseline, because deleting agents/roadmaps/road-to-council-topology-evidence-followups.md produces 38 of those and must red immediately rather than nudge a count. REMEDY WHEN THE 56-DAY NON-STAGNATION CLAUSE FIRES (from `landed`, i.e. 2026-10-28), named here because neither remedy the checker prints fits this population: "fix the findings" is ruled out by the sentence above -- rewriting an archived roadmap's step semantics retroactively invents an intent nobody recorded -- and "lower the count" is ruled out with it, since this population only shrinks when an owner decides one entry at a time. The remedy that fits is a `reaffirmed: {date, reason}` block on THIS entry (`_lib/gate_baseline.ts`), whose reason lands in the diff of the change that makes it: that is the path for debt which is genuinely unrepairable rather than merely unattended. A reaffirmation is not automatic. It asserts that the 243 were re-read and are still unrepairable, and if any of them has become repairable in the meantime the count goes down instead. Do not reaffirm at age 0 -- the clause exists so the question is asked once every 56 days, and answering it early answers nothing.

lint_roadmap_blockers:decidability.note:
Open blocker entries that are not yet DECIDABLE by the person who owns them — missing `Recommendation:` (which option and why), missing `If you do nothing:` (the cost of the non-decision), or a `What to do:` carrying no command, path or enumerated option set. Revealed by adding the decidability half to lint_roadmap_blockers, not created by it: the five original fields describe a situation and never made it actionable, so a blocker could pass the contract while handing the analysis back to the person least equipped to redo it. Measured at introduction: 36 open entries, ALL 36 undecidable, and 14 of the 46 total entries carry no command/path/option at all in `What to do`. Baselined rather than hard-failed because 36 findings nobody can clear in the change that reveals them is the gate-that-lands-as-N-instant-blockers failure this repository has refused before — the same reasoning as ci-parity:local-only above. First measured at 34 rather than 36 because the two blockers on the branch that introduced this (`ac3-false-positive-reading`, `publish-side-marker-invariant`) were rewritten to the new standard and then closed in the same change; a baseline above the truth silently permits new violations. Re-measured at 38 when the branch was re-pointed at current main, and the +4 is population growth rather than a loosening: main gained the four `road-to-inbox-harvest-2026-08-d-*` roadmaps (context-ledger, runtime-skill-routing, scheduled-deprecation, top-band-model-economy), each carrying one open blocker authored before this requirement existed. That is the honest number for the population this gate now scans — recording 34 against a 38-entry tree would have failed the gate on its own introducing commit and taught the next reader to distrust it. Lowering happens one blocker at a time, and every roadmap touched for other reasons is a chance to lower it. Lowered 38→37 by the scheduled-deprecation PR, which is exactly that shape: code-graph-removal-authorisation was rewritten to the new standard because the roadmap was being touched anyway. Its `If you do nothing:` was one of the few that was not the common no-cost answer — the release gate that PR ships would have refused the next major cut while the blocker stayed open. Recorded in the past tense because the maintainer then RESOLVED that blocker on the trunk by withdrawing the commitment, so nothing refuses a cut today. The lowering stands on the rewrite, not on the consequence, and the sentence is corrected rather than deleted because a baseline note arguing from a retracted state is how a ratchet's rationale rots. The 56-day expiry is the point, not a hazard: if this number has not moved in two months, the fields are not being written and the gate should fail until someone decides whether the requirement is real. Lowered 37→34 when the scheduled-deprecation branch merged current main: three blockers were resolved or rewritten on the trunk in the meantime, so the drop is a genuine drain plus a merge, not a loosening. Re-tightened here rather than left loose because a ratchet that lags its own tree permits violations back in silently. Lowered 34→29 on 2026-08-16 by rewriting six entries to the new standard (raw-capture-needs-host-env, telemetry-sample-size, repo-admin-and-usage, benchmark-spend, measurement-a-no-per-arm-builder-tier, measurement-b-no-renderable-lane-pair) in a PR whose only purpose was the drain — the first lowering not taken on the back of another change, which the note above says is the usual shape. Two findings from that pass are worth keeping. The tree measured 35 against a baseline of 34 BEFORE the drain, i.e. the ratchet was already red on main and nobody knew: this gate runs in `task ci`, no workflow invokes `task ci`, and the local run that would have shown it was read through a `tail`, which hid every row above the last six. And four of the six `If you do nothing:` answers are honestly that nothing degrades — that is the true answer for a held measurement, and writing it is what makes the entry decidable, so the field earns its place by being cheap to answer truthfully rather than by always carrying a cost. Lowered 29 → 27 on 2026-08-16 by the merge of this branch and the trunk drain above, and the arithmetic matters more than the delta: both sides rewrote entries from the same tree of 35 independently — the trunk six (recorded above), this branch two (deferred-finding-decision-reopen, spent-inbox-artifacts-await-deletion, rewritten because road-to-inbox-harvest-residuals was being touched anyway). The sets are disjoint, so the merged tree measures 27 and the gate itself reported the slack. Tightened rather than banked: 29 against a 27-entry tree would absorb the next two undecidable blockers without anything noticing, which is the lag this note has now corrected twice. Lowered 27 → 26 on 2026-08-16 by rewriting `picktier-wire-or-archive` (road-to-inbox-harvest-2026-08-d-top-band-model-economy), and this one is the usual shape the note describes rather than the dedicated-drain shape: the roadmap was being worked for its own Step 4.1 and the entry was rewritten because it was open on the desk. Worth recording for what writing the two fields SURFACED, which is the argument for the requirement: `Recommendation:` forced the question 'which option, and why' and the honest answer turned out not to be one of the three options at all — the entry defers to a converged council verdict, and the council cannot reach quorum (re-measured 0 of 2 the same day), so the actionable next step is a one-line fix to a user-global config file outside this repository. Five fields had described that situation accurately for two weeks without anyone noticing that the named blocker was infrastructure rather than judgement. Lowered 26 → 22 on 2026-08-18 by road-to-estate-drawdown Step 0.1, which needed the two fields for a different reason and therefore drained six entries as a by-product: the consolidated decision sheet renders a DEFAULT plus that default's provenance per user-owned decision, and 7 of the 21 live entries recorded no `Recommendation:` to derive one from. Six were rewritten to the new standard (skill-activation-window, b-convergence-machine, maintainer-blind-ratings, real-orchestration-usage, human-gated-live-trigger-eval, manual-rubric-rater), each marked `agent-drafted` in the field itself so the sheet can label the provenance rather than presenting a drafted default beside a maintainer-recorded one as the same kind of statement. The seventh, `road-to-gated-reach-followup`'s legacy `> Blocked until …` note, is NOT counted here and was not rewritten: it is a blocked-until note rather than a `### blocker:` entry, so it has no field to carry, and converting it is a roadmap restructure this change did not take. **The tree was RED at 28 against this baseline of 26 before the drain, and again nobody knew** — the same failure the 34→29 paragraph above records, one gate cycle later: two entries had been added on the trunk without the fields, and this gate runs in `task ci`, which no workflow invokes. That is the second recorded instance of this ratchet being red on main undetected, which is an argument about where it runs rather than about its number. `human-gated-live-trigger-eval` also gained a command in `What to do:` (`rule_trigger_eval`, verified to exist at src/scripts/) because the field carried a path-less instruction; the other five needed only the two decidability fields. Lowered 22 -> 20 on 2026-08-19 by road-to-estate-drawdown Phase 2 triage batch 1, and RE-MEASURED after two merges of origin/main rather than carried over: the trunk gained roadmaps in between (the long-horizon pair and the council-fallback set), and the live count over the merged tree is still 20 across 39 roadmaps. Six roadmaps moved to later/, and two of them carried an undecidable open blocker each. The gain is a side effect of parking rather than of drafting a recommendation, so it is recorded as such — the two entries are unchanged and still undecidable where they sit; they are simply outside the active tree this ratchet scans. Walked down because the gate reported itself loose, and a baseline above the measurement is headroom a later change can spend with nothing objecting. Lowered 20 -> 17 on 2026-08-20 by the road-to-frontend-skill-application closeout, and the shape is the usual one this note describes: the roadmap was being closed for its own reasons and its three open blockers were on the desk anyway. Two (ui-corpus-has-no-ui, enforcement-evidence) left the population by being RESOLVED rather than rewritten, which is the cleanest way to lower this number and the only one that does not add prose; the third (ui-session-capture-window) was rewritten to the new standard. Worth recording what writing the two fields surfaced, since that is the standing argument for the requirement: on ui-corpus-has-no-ui, `Recommendation:` forced the question "which option, and why" and the honest answer was that the entry's own premise was false — it asserted the question could not be answered without a human naming a consumer store, and the stores were already on the machine, readable by the command the entry itself printed. Five fields had described that situation accurately for a week without anyone noticing the blocker was a measurement nobody had run. Tightened rather than banked because 20 against a 17-entry tree is headroom the next three undecidable blockers would spend with nothing objecting, which is the lag the paragraphs above have now corrected three times. Walked 17 -> 12 at the drain/road-to-frontend-skill-application merge, 2026-08-21, on the gate's own loose-ratchet report. Re-measured against the merged tree rather than attributed: sibling drain PRs made entries decidable in parallel, so this branch's share is not separable here and is not claimed. Banked at the measurement rather than left as headroom a later change could spend.

WALKED 12 -> 1 on 2026-08-22 by resolving the two `road-to-evidence-based-adr-governance` blockers (`owner-autonomy-batch`, `authority-coupling-decision`), which were undecidable in exactly the way this ratchet names: each handed a Hard-Floor question to the reader without a landed outcome. Both now carry one. The single remaining violation is `road-to-drain-commands:395` (`merge-authority`), which PR #1517 resolves and archives — so the honest count for THIS tree is 1 and it is expected to reach 0 once that lands. It is not lowered to 0 here, because a baseline must describe the tree it ships with rather than the tree someone expects next. Lowered 1 -> 0 on 2026-08-22, and the prediction the previous entry made is what closed it: the single remaining violation was `road-to-drain-commands:395` (`merge-authority`), and PR #1517 archived that roadmap, taking the entry out of the scanned population. Nothing was rewritten to reach zero -- the record left the active tree with its blocker RESOLVED, which is the cleanest of the two ways this number goes down and the only one that adds no prose. Zero is now the ceiling: any new open blocker missing `Recommendation:`, `If you do nothing:` or an actionable `What to do:` reds this gate immediately, with no headroom at all.
lint_roadmap_blockers:decidability.retired_because: Walked to 0 and therefore removed from `gates`: an entry recording no debt is what gate_baseline.test.ts refuses, and a missing entry is not weaker — evaluateGate treats an absent baseline as ok only when the live count is 0, which is the same ceiling the note below asked for. Kept here because the note is dated history, not commentary; nothing reads this key at runtime.
